newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire government agrees Eurocan copper deal.
newsitem.headline: Zaire government agrees Eurocan copper deal.

text.p: Zaire's government agreed a major deal on mining copper and cobalt in its southern region of Shaba with Canadian mining and exploration company Consolidated Eurocan Ventures Ltd on Friday, spokesmen for both sides said.

The Kinshasa representative of the Lundin group and Geneva-based Swedish financier Adolf Lundin, who were negotiating on behalf of Eurocan, told Reuters the deal would be signed with state-run mining company Gecamines on Saturday.
Lundin group's Saidi Mbongo said he had seen a copy of the contract letter signed by the deputy prime minister in charge of mines after Friday's cabinet meeting.
Earlier, government spokesman Boguo Makeli said that the cabinet had reached a "conclusive decision". Asked if had agreed the Lundin-proposed offer, he replied, "It goes in that direction."
Under the deal, Gecamines will have a 45 percent stake in the project at Tenke Fungurume and Eurocan a 55 percent stake, sources close to the deal said.
Lundin group had a 55 percent stake in Eurocan, they added.
